title: Fri 6 Nov: Nifty's sixth straight gain meets a Wall Street rout
description:
Hot topic: the Nifty rose for a sixth straight day on record foreign buying, then Wall Street had its worst day since April 2025. Then: Airtel, Titan, ONGC, oil, the rupee, US payrolls, foreign flows, IT and IndiGo.

1. Nifty jumps 2.4% to 24,537 for a sixth straight gain as foreign investors buy 14,975 crore rupees (Business Today)
2. Bharti Airtel's ARPU climbs to 271 rupees, but profit of 8,888 crore rupees misses estimates (Upstox)
3. Titan's jewellery sales grow 24%; board approves 2,500 crore rupees of NCDs (Upstox)
4. ONGC's standalone profit jumps 57% to 15,489 crore rupees; record 8 rupee interim dividend (Upstox)
5. Brent rebounds 3.88% to 98.29 dollars as Iran peace remains unconfirmed (Reuters via Yahoo Finance)
6. Rupee ends flat at 94.46 as foreign inflows offset a firmer dollar (HDFC Sky (PTI))
7. US payrolls are the next test after Treasury yields slide to their lowest since September (Stock Titan)
8. Foreign investors buy a net 14,975 crore rupees, a fifth straight day, as banks lead the rally (NiftyTrader)
9. IT stocks rebound 2.4% even as the Nasdaq slides on AI-regulation worries (Stock Titan)
10. IndiGo and Asian Paints jump 4-5% as the oil slide lifts fuel-sensitive stocks (DSIJ)

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated with open-source Kokoro voices. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm P.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm S. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Today's big one: the Nifty's six-day rally runs straight into Wall Street's worst day since April 2025.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: S, start with Thursday at home.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nifty closed at 24,536.60, up 2.40%. That's a sixth straight gain. Foreign investors bought a net 14,975 crore rupees of shares.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who led it?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Banks. Nifty Bank jumped 3.33%, and HDFC Bank rose 3.16% to 760 rupees. IT joined in, with Nifty IT up 2.42%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And then America happened.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It did. The Nasdaq fell 5.52% and the S&P 500 4.36%, on fears a Democratic Congress will slow the AI data-centre build-out.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: This morning Japan's Nikkei fell about 6%, and Korea's Kospi plunged more than 8%. GIFT Nifty pointed to a lower open.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Six days up. Does one bad night in New York really matter here?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. This rally rested on foreign buying. If global risk appetite cracks, that money can leave, and the biggest bank weights feel it first.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What's the trigger to watch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Whether foreign investors stay net buyers and the Nifty holds 24,000. Heavy foreign selling would send it back below.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Reliance. Sentiment: negative.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: Airtel beats on ARPU but misses on profit.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Revenue rose 16.7% to 60,878 crore rupees. ARPU came in at 271 rupees, against 268 to 269 expected.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: But profit of 8,888 crore rupees missed the 9,209 crore in a CNBC-TV18 poll.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Which number wins?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: ARPU drives telecom valuations, and the EBITDA margin was a strong 57.4%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: this shows which line investors pay for in Indian telecom. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea, Indus Towers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: Titan's jewellery growth cools a little.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Jewellery sales grew 24%, below the 27 to 28% Kotak Neo expected. Income rose about 25%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Reports of the profit figure differ, so we'll skip it. The board approved 2,500 crore rupees of NCDs.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Titan is the bellwether for festive jewellery demand into Dhanteras and Diwali. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, Senco Gold.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: ONGC's profit jumps, with a record dividend.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Standalone profit rose 57.3% to about 15,489 crore rupees, on revenue of 43,875 crore. The board declared an 8 rupee interim dividend.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The stock fell 2.13% to 230 rupees on Thursday, before oil turned back up overnight.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: an oil rebound and a record dividend both support upstream names after a sharp fall. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: ONGC, Oil India.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: oil bounces right back.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent settled up 3.88% at 98.29 dollars. WTI rose 2.72% to 90.52 dollars.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What flipped it?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: UKMTO counted at least five vessels hit in the Gulf since Sunday. Eurasia Group cut its odds of a US-Iran deal to 10%, from 20%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: oil above 95 dollars feeds India's import bill, the rupee and inflation. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: IndiGo, BPCL, Asian Paints.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: the rupee holds its ground.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The rupee settled unchanged at 94.46 per dollar, as record foreign inflows offset a firmer dollar.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Can that last?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Dearer oil and a global sell-off usually pressure the rupee. A move above 94.6 would be the warning sign.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the rupee sets India's oil import cost and the return on foreign money here. Sentiment: neutral. Stocks in focus: Infosys, IndiGo.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: US jobs data lands tonight. Why should I care?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.84%, from 4.89%. December Fed-hike odds dropped to 70.1%, from 82.7%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: ADP showed 86,000 private jobs, and jobless claims fell to a 57-year low.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And if the number comes in hot?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: A strong payrolls surprise would send yields sharply higher and revive the hike odds.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: payrolls decide whether the Fed hikes in December, which sets global yields and foreign flows into India. Sentiment: mixed.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: foreign money, a fifth straight day.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Foreign investors were net buyers for a fifth straight day on Thursday, and banks led the rally.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Is today the day that streak breaks?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's the test. Friday's open follows the worst US session since April 2025 and steep falls in Tokyo and Seoul.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a reversal would hit the largest bank weights first. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Kotak Bank, Axis Bank.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: Indian IT rallied, then the Nasdaq crashed.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Infosys rose 3.48% to 1,167.40 rupees, and Nifty IT gained 2.42% on Thursday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Overnight, UBS said about 30% of data-centre additions expected in 2028 are now at risk.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Indian IT now trades on US tech sentiment and AI policy. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS, HCLTech, Wipro.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Last one. Story ten: IndiGo and Asian Paints flew on cheap oil.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: IndiGo rose 5.43% to 5,420 rupees and Asian Paints 4.36%, after Brent's 8.7% fall.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And now oil is back up?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Yes. Brent settled 3.88% higher overnight after new tanker attacks, which puts those gains at risk.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: fuel is an airline's biggest cost, and crude feeds paint inputs. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: IndiGo, Asian Paints, Berger Paints.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch today: foreign flows at the open, whether the Nifty holds 24,000, and US payrolls tonight.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
